result.markdown:
When dealing with a slip and fall injury in a shopping centre, you need a public liability lawyer who understands New South Wales premises liability law (such as the Civil Liability Act) and has a track record of dealing with major corporate entities and insurance companies.

Several well-regarded law firms handle public liability and slip-and-fall claims in the Newcastle and Hunter region:

### Prominent Local and Regional Firms in Newcastle

* **Whitelaw McDonald Lawyers:** Located in Kotara (right near Westfield Kotara), they have deep roots in the Newcastle community spanning over 40 years.[wmcdlaw.com.au](https://wmcdlaw.com.au/compensation-law/personal-injury-permanent-disability/#:~:text=It%20can%20be%20especially%20stressful%20when%20the,Call%20%2802%29%204941%208970.%20Make%20an%20Enquiry.) Notably, they have historic public liability experience handling major retail slip-and-fall cases. They feature Law Society Accredited Specialists in Personal Injury Law.[wmcdlaw.com.au](https://wmcdlaw.com.au/compensation-law/personal-injury-permanent-disability/#:~:text=Matthew%20Berenger.%20Principal%20Director%20%E2%80%93%20Accredited%20Specialist,Bechelli.%20Senior%20Associate%20%E2%80%93%20Personal%20Injury%20Law.)
* **The Law Office of Conrad Curry:** Led by Accredited Personal Injury Specialists, this firm is locally based in Newcastle and frequently handles public liability claims involving injuries sustained in shopping centres, public spaces, and private premises.[conradcurrylaw.com.au](https://conradcurrylaw.com.au/personal-injury-lawyers-newcastle/#:~:text=We%20handle%20claims%20for%20injuries%20sustained%20in,you%20deserve%20in%20accordance%20with%20NSW%20law.)

### Established National & Statewide Firms with Newcastle Offices

* **Shine Lawyers (Newcastle Office on King Street):** A large national personal injury firm with a dedicated local team handling public liability, slip-and-fall, and occupier's liability claims.[www.shine.com.au](https://www.shine.com.au/locations/nsw/newcastle#:~:text=As%20part%20of%20our%20national%20team%2C%20Shine,child%2C%20including%20historical%20child%20sex%20abuse%20compensation.)
* **LHD Lawyers (Newcastle):** Another major firm servicing the Hunter region that handles public liability and complex compensation cases on a regional basis.
* **Stacks Goudkamp (Hunter Street, Newcastle):** Highly regarded for personal injury and public liability claims, featuring accredited specialists with extensive courtroom and negotiation experience against large insurers.[stacklaw.com.au](https://stacklaw.com.au/location/newcastle#:~:text=Tom%20has%20been%20a%20pre-eminent%20personal%20injury,standard%20in%20compensation%20and%20personal%20injury%20law.)

---

### What to Look For & Key Questions to Ask

Before choosing a lawyer, it is wise to consult with two or three of them for an initial discussion (most offer a free case evaluation). Keep the following in mind:

1.  **No Win, No Fee Arrangement:** Ensure they operate on a **"No Win, No Fee"** basis.[www.shine.com.au](https://www.shine.com.au/locations/nsw/newcastle#:~:text=Fees.%20Ensuring%20everyone%20has%20access%20to%20justice,on%20a%20No%20Win%2C%20No%20Fee*%20basis.) Clarify how disbursements (out-of-pocket costs like medical reports or barrister fees) are handled if the claim is unsuccessful.
2.  **Accredited Specialist:** Look for lawyers who are **Law Society Accredited Specialists in Personal Injury Law**. This designation means they have undergone rigorous testing and peer review to prove a high level of expertise in this specific field.
3.  **Shopping Centre Experience:** Ask specifically if they have successfully resolved claims against major retail landlords or shopping centre management companies (e.g., Scentre Group, Stockland, GPT, etc.), as these cases often involve complex contractual and occupier liability defenses.

### Immediate Steps for Your Claim

* **Report the Incident:** Ensure you (or someone on your behalf) filled out an incident report with shopping centre management and requested a copy.
* **Gather Evidence:** Keep photos of the hazard (e.g., a wet floor without a sign, a broken tile), your footwear, and your injuries. Keep all medical certificates and receipts for expenses.
* **Time Limits:** In NSW, personal injury and public liability claims generally have strict time limits (often a 3-year limitation period from the date of the injury, though earlier notification is vital).

Are you still receiving medical treatment for your injuries, or have you already reported the incident to the shopping centre management?
